file_name.description: The name of the file to which the generated image will be saved. It should include the file extension, such as 'image.png'.

content.description: The HTML content to be written to the file. Must contain valid HTML structure.

function.description: Executes a search query using the DuckDuckGo search engine and returns a specified number of search results from a given source. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

query.description: The search term or phrase to be queried.

num_results.description: The maximum number of search results to return. A positive integer.

source.description: The source from which the search results should be fetched.

function.name: get_url_content
function.description: Scrapes the specified URL for textual data and returns the content as a string. This function is useful for extracting information from web pages when a URL is provided. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The web address of the page to scrape. It should be a valid URL format, such as 'http://www.example.com'.

message.content:
Below is a quick‑start guide for launching a **Google Cloud Compute Engine** instance that has an **RTX A6000** GPU and runs **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**.  
(If you’re actually looking for an AWS EC2 command, let me know – the syntax would be different.)

---

## 1️⃣ Using the `gcloud` CLI

```bash
# 1. Pick a zone that supports the RTX A6000 (e.g. us-central1-a)
ZONE="us-central1-a"

# 2. Create a new VM instance
gcloud compute instances create my-rtx-a6000 \
    --zone=$ZONE \
    --machine-type=n1-standard-8 \          # 8 vCPUs, 30 GB RAM
    --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
    --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
    --boot-disk-size=100GB \
    --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
    --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1 \
    --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \
    --restart-on-failure \
    --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh   # optional init script
```

> **Notes**  
> * Replace `my-rtx-a6000` with your preferred instance name.  
> * Adjust `--machine-type` if you need more or fewer CPUs/RAM.  
> * The `--accelerator` flag attaches one RTX A6000 GPU.  
> * Ensure you have the **NVIDIA GPU Driver** installed on the instance (you can add a startup script that installs the driver automatically).

---

## 2️⃣ Using the REST API (JSON payload)

If you prefer to use the raw REST endpoint, here’s a minimal JSON body you could POST to:

```json
{
  "name": "my-rtx-a6000",
  "machineType": "zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/zones/us-central1-a/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [{ "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }]
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorType": "projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000",
      "acceleratorCount": 1
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\nsudo apt-get update\nsudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Send this payload to:

```
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/zones/us-central1-a/instances
Authorization: Bearer YOUR_OAUTH_TOKEN
Content-Type: application/json
```

Replace `YOUR_PROJECT_ID` and `YOUR_OAUTH_TOKEN` with your actual project ID and OAuth bearer token.

---

## 3️⃣ Quick sanity check

After creation, verify the GPU is visible:

```bash
gcloud compute ssh my-rtx-a6000 --zone=$ZONE --command="nvidia-smi"
```

You should see the RTX A6000 listed with its driver version.

---

### Want a ready‑to‑run startup script?

Here’s a simple `startup.sh` you can reference in the `--metadata-from-file` flag:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Update & install NVIDIA driver
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535
# Install CUDA Toolkit (optional)
wget https://developer.download.nvidia.com/compute/cuda/repos/ubuntu2004/x86_64/cuda-ubuntu2004.pin
sudo mv cuda-ubuntu2004.pin /etc/apt/preferences.d/cuda-repository-pin-600
wget http://developer.download.nvidia.com/compute/cuda/12.1.0/local_installers/cuda-repo-ubuntu2004-12-1-local_12.1.0-525.60.13-1_amd64.deb
sudo dpkg -i cuda-repo-ubuntu2004-12-1-local_12.1.0-525.60.13-1_amd64.deb
sudo cp /var/cuda-repo-ubuntu2004-12-1-local/cuda-*-keyring.gpg /usr/share/keyrings/
sudo apt-key add /var/cuda-repo-ubuntu2004-12-1-local/cuda-*-keyring.gpg
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y cuda
```

Feel free to tweak the machine type, disk size, or GPU count to match your workload. Happy GPU computing!
